summary: Gérard Huet works in computational linguistics and indology. He studied under George Ernst (circa 1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (circa 1972–1976), and became a professor at Inria around 1974.

Géza Bethlenfalvy was an indologist and tibetologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under János Harmatta and Lajos Ligeti. His career included posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Delhi (1970), and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Géza Uray was a tibetologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Lajos Ligeti in 1942. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (1948–1949, 1979), the Research Centre for Linguistics (circa 1953–1973), and the University of Pennsylvania (1973–1984).

Gösta Liebert was an indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Gothenburg and Lund University under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held professorships at Uppsala University (1951–1953) and the University of Gothenburg (1955–1982).

Götz von Selle was an Iranian, Central Asian, and historical scholar who studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. circa 1918–1920). He served as a librarian at Göttingen and became an honorary professor and library director at Königsberg in 1939.
Günter Blamberger held posts at the University of Kassel (circa 1991–1995) and became Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne around 1995.

Günter Grönbold worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (circa 1964–1969). He spent his career at the Bavarian State Library (circa 1974–2008), heading its Oriental Section from circa 1988 to 2008.

Religious studies scholar Günter Lanczkowski studied at the University of Göttingen and the University of Marburg, earning a PhD in 1947. He served as Privatdocent at Heidelberg University (1960–1982) and taught religion at Mainz (1984–1986) and Munich (1986–1988).

Günter Schweiger studied under Gert Klingenschmitt and at the Vienna University of Economics and Business, where he served as a full professor from 1974 to 2009. His field of scholarship includes linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies.

Günther Schulemann worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying in Berlin, Freiburg, and Breslau (Ph.D. circa 1910–1913), he served as Privatdozent (1923) and associate professor of philosophy (1930–1939) at the University of Breslau.

Günther Weibgen was an indologist who studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders from circa 1920 to 1925. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin beginning in 1928, becoming Oberbibliothekar in 1944.

Günther-Dietz Sontheimer studied in Tübingen, Pune, and SOAS under scholars including Helmuth von Glasenapp and J. Duncan M. Derrett. Working in Indology, religious studies, and history, he spent his academic career at Heidelberg University from 1965 until 1979 as professor.

Linguist H. Craig Melchert studied under Calvert Watkins at Harvard University (circa 1972–1977). He held faculty positions at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari was an indologist who studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where he completed an MA under C. Kunhan Raja. By 1944, he was attested as a Research Assistant at Adyar Library and Research Centre.
H. J. de Graaf worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (circa 1919–1926) and studied under Poerbatjaraka from 1927 to 1930.
H. Kikuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, and was attested in 1966 as a research student at the University of Delhi studying under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale.

H. Munro Chadwick was a scholar of linguistics, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Cambridge and under Wilhelm Streitberg, he was a Fellow and Librarian at Clare College and Cambridge's Elrington and Bosworth Professor of Anglo-Saxon (1910–1941).

H. Schöhl was an indologist and linguist who studied at several universities, including Strasbourg, Freiburg, Munich, Göttingen, and Münster. He studied under Ernst Leumann and completed a PhD under Richard Schmidt at Münster (circa 1912–1914).
H. Sesha Aiyangar worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts in the Kannaḍa and Canarese departments at the University of Madras, attested in 1938 and 1957.

H. V. Nagaraja Rao worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Pandit at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, held a post at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore, and was attested as a professor at the University of Mysore in 2012.
